caption:
The Trump administration plans to name more than two dozen US companies as AI "national champions," The Wall Street Journal reported.
Nvidia, Amazon, Microsoft, OpenAI and Anthropic are among them.
The goal is to sell American AI packages abroad and beat Chinese rivals like Huawei, with faster export licenses and federal financing for the chosen firms.

Should the government pick winners in AI?

paragraphs.text: The Trump administration is preparing to designate more than two dozen American companies as national champions in artificial intelligence, The Wall Street Journal reported on Sunday, November 15, 2026. Nvidia, Amazon, Microsoft, OpenAI and Anthropic are among the companies expected to receive the label, according to summaries of the report by The Next Web and Open Magazine.

The full list has not been made public. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick is expected to unveil it, and an announcement could come within the next week, although the timing could still change, according to the reports.

The plan is built on the American AI Exports Program, which was created by an executive order signed on July 23, 2025. Under the program, the Commerce Department encourages groups of companies to offer full American AI packages abroad, combining chips, models, cloud capacity and related products so that foreign governments and businesses can buy them in one deal. The Next Web reported that Commerce said in July 2026 that industry groups had filed 78 applications.

According to outlines of the program on the Commerce Department's portal, designated packages may receive faster reviews of export license applications, government advocacy and support for overseas projects, and access to federal financing. The reports did not describe any new obligations for the companies that are chosen.

Coinpedia described the roles of the five named companies in such packages: Nvidia would supply chips, OpenAI and Anthropic would provide AI models, and Amazon and Microsoft would provide cloud and data center infrastructure.

The stated aim is to persuade foreign governments and companies to adopt US-developed AI systems instead of Chinese alternatives. Open Magazine named Huawei Technologies, which has been expanding in Europe and Latin America, as one of the competitors the program is meant to counter. The Next Web noted that Chinese state media said in October that Beijing had cleared DeepSeek and MiniMax to take their models overseas.

The list is expected to arrive during the week President Trump travels to China. He is scheduled to attend the APEC summit in Shenzhen on November 18 and 19 and to meet Chinese leader Xi Jinping there, and Lutnick is set to accompany him, according to the reports.

The designation comes at a difficult moment for Nvidia. Jensen Huang resigned as chief executive on November 12 after admitting an affair with a woman whom US officials suspect of spying for China, The Next Web reported. Critics have argued that national security should come before market share, and some lawmakers and officials are concerned that Chinese companies are obtaining advanced Nvidia chips through gaps in export controls.

Critics have accused the Commerce Department of failing to close those gaps, and The Wall Street Journal previously reported that Lutnick was wary of angering Beijing during trade talks, according to The Next Web. Open Magazine reported that Commerce is also expected to advance new rules against the illegal diversion of high-performance processors to China.

The label would formalize what has been an informal relationship between Washington and its largest AI suppliers. Putting OpenAI and Anthropic on the same list as Nvidia, Amazon and Microsoft signals that the administration sees frontier models, not only chips, as an export product to be promoted abroad. The timing also ties the program closely to the questions now surrounding Nvidia and to the trade talks with Beijing.
The next step to watch is the official list from the Commerce Department, which should show which other companies were chosen and whether new conditions on chip sales to China are attached.
